To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis of polymerizable redox‐active metal bipyridine complexes and their use as both crosslinkers and redox‐catalysts for the BZ reaction in poly(N‐isoproprylacrylamides) hydrogels leads to new materials with unique chemomechanical properties, which may be of interest for the development of novel functional devices.

we have developed a new family of redox‐responsive polymerizable bipyriidine ligands and their metal complexes that can be used as both crosslinkers and redox‐responsive catalysts for self‐oscillatory Belousov– Zhabotinskii reaction.

the synthesis of a new library of Ru and Iron complexes containing polymerizable bipydine ligands is described, and that these complexes have been used to prepare a new class of redox‐responsive hydrogels that exhibit chemomechanical self‐oscillation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing new functional materials with dynamic properties that are based on self‐oscillatory Belousov– Zhabotinskii reactions and their coupling with the redox chemistry of Ru(II) and Fe(II) complexes of the type [M(bpy) _{2} ] ^{2+}.
the design and preparation of new redox‐active metal bipyridine complexes that are suitable for use as both crosslinkers and redox‐catalysts in polymerization reactions of hydrophilic monomers.

the development of a new class of redox‐responsive, self‐oscillatory, and chemomechanically switchable gels that may be used in a wide variety of applications, including sensors, actuators, and drug delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work provides a new approach to the development of redox‐responsive gels that are able to switch their swelling/contractions mode depending on the oxidation state and the redox potential of the crosslinker.

the redox‐active Ru(II) bipyridine complexes can be used as both a cross‐linking agent and a catalyst in the synthesis of self‐oscillatory hydrogels, and their redox state can be tuned by external stimuli to modulate the swelling behavior of the gels.

the new redox‐active Ru complexes with bipyridine‐containing ligands are promising candidates for use in a variety of applications, including catalysis, molecular electronics, and stimuli‐responsive materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new class of redox‐responsive crosslinkers that can be incorporated into a wide variety of polymer networks, including those of hydrophilic and hydrophobic nature, and can induce self‐oscillatory BZ chemistry in such networks.
the new redox‐responsive hydrogels are the first examples of the materials that can undergo swelling‐contraction cycles in response to the BZ reaction.

the redox‐active Ru complexes, as a crosslinker, are able to control the swelling/contraction modes of the gels, and this is the first example of a chemomechanical switch based on the redox‐induced conformational change of the metal complexes in the gel network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the swelling/contraction of redox‐responsive hydrogels can be tuned by changing the ratio of the comonomers, and that such materials can be used to create new functional modules for smart, self‐oscillatory devices.

the swelling/contraction behavior of the gels may be controlled by the choice of the redox‐active crosslinker and the composition of the gel network, which opens up a new avenue for designing chemomechanically responsive materials.
by choosing the appropriate comonomers and metal complexes, the swelling trends of redox‐responsive gels can be inverted.
